vq_steps: Living in Edinburgh, Vision is hunted by the bounty hunter Paladin and rescues Tommy, who claims to be his son.
Shot with adamantium rounds, Vision loses J.A.R.V.I.S., then has Tommy restart his failing core in a motel pool.
To stop the Butcherbird Killer, Vision lets Ultron take control, but Ultron locks him out and leaves with Tommy.
Vision drops his firewalls to retake his body, setting Ultron free, and wakes with Lisa on a cargo plane to Madripoor.
In Madripoor, Vision fights the Ten Rings beside Paladin and tells Tommy the truth about Westview and his memories.
Deep in his own code, Vision accepts he is the one Vision and Tommy his son, saves Lisa, and gives himself up to the Client.
Freed by Tommy, Vision traps a grieving Ultron in a sitcom and talks him down, and Tommy and Billy restart his burned out core.
Vision says goodbye to his AIs, takes a call from Ultron, and leaves his Mindspace to meet his sons in New Jersey.

k: A synthezoid born from J.A.R.V.I.S. and the Mind Stone
A rebuilt white Vision with his old memories
The one Vision, father to Tommy and Billy

existing.notes: One person across the app: the wiki splits him into Vision (the original, killed in Infinity War), Vision/Chaos Magic Recreation (the Westview Vision Wanda made) and White Vision (the rebuilt body that leaves Westview). VisionQuest's lead is the wiki's White Vision; the original and the Westview Vision are only archive footage (eps 1, 2, 3, 6, 7), plus the original as a memory he argues with in ep 7. In ep 7 he accepts he is all three ('There is only one, and I am he'), which is the new k stage; the existing rf white-vision handover (C, R, C) still fits. Old step 1 named Jocasta in an ep 4 step, but the name is first said in ep 6 (Ultron, 'Jocasta'), so it now says the Butcherbird Killer; its ep tag was also wrong (6, now 4). Sherwood Ellis is his human alias, said in ep 1 (Fiona and Paladin). Groups: the screen names no new group in ep 8 (the recaps call Paladin's new venture 'bounty givers', not a name), so Independent holds. Episode 8 has no transcript: its steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and the Wikipedia summary.

vq_steps: After a near drowning fills his head with Tommy Maximoff's memories, Thomas escapes a bus to Saint Mabyn's with Lisa.
Grifting London crowds with Lisa, Thomas sees Vision on the news and panics, and Paladin snatches him off the street.
Held at Saint Mabyn's as bait, Thomas is freed by Vision, and when Paladin shoots Vision, he refuses to leave him.
Told his memories are a delusion, Thomas finds he can phase, then uses his speed to restart Vision in a pool.
Thomas gets Lisa to sneak them into Katerina Wells's gala, learns Vision hid Ultron, and goes off with Ultron in Vision's body.
After a pint with Ultron, Thomas is snatched by Paladin and taken to Madripoor with what he is told is a bomb in his arm.
Thomas and Lisa take Paladin's van to save Vision and share a kiss, and his speed shuts down Jocasta's nanobot in her.
Thomas tells Vision he loves Lisa, then reads Vision's letter calling him his son as Paladin hands Vision to the Client.
Now going by Tommy, he nearly drowns himself to reach Billy, then races through Virgil Horton's house to free Vision and Jocasta.
Tommy and Billy restart Vision together, and Tommy flies to New Jersey with Lisa and Paladin for a family dinner.

k: A London grifter called Thomas Shepherd
Vision's speedster son, now going by Tommy

existing.notes: Both old steps replaced: step 0 called him a pickpocket (Lisa is the pickpocket, he is the grifter) and he never claims to be Vision's son to Paladin (Paladin finds the police report); step 1 was two sentences, over length, and its ep tag key pointed at a step that did not exist. Story order puts the Christmas 2027 bus escape (ep 2) first. He is Thomas in VisionQuest until ep 8, where the recaps say he now calls himself Tommy, hence the k stage. Paladin's 'Speed' line in ep 6 is a joke about the movie, not an alias. Ep 5 shows him only in Ultron's recorded pub talk, folded into the Madripoor step. Episode 8 has no transcript: its steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and the Wikipedia summary. Name check: Thomas said ep 1 ('Thomas, I could have'), Thomas Shepherd ep 1, Tommy ep 1 (the WandaVision son) and ep 2 ('Tommy.' 'Thomas. My name's Thomas.'), Lisa ep 1, Saint Mabyn's ep 2, Katerina Wells ep 4, Madripoor ep 5, Jocasta ep 6 (not ep 4), Billy and Virgil Horton ep 8; every step uses each only from then. 'Now going by Tommy' in ep 8 rests on Den of Geek ('now calling himself Tommy'), with Laughing Place switching to Tommy from his talk with Billy.

vq_steps: Dream binding from New Jersey, Billy meets Tommy while he is nearly drowned, but says he is still bad at portals.
Billy reaches England in time to help Tommy restart Vision, who answers his offered handshake with a hug.
existing.notes: No VisionQuest steps before. Judged on lines and part (a new version of him): ep 8 has both, played by the Agatha All Along actor. Eps 1, 3, 6 and 7 hold only WandaVision footage, child voices and an ep 7 illusion of two children, so no step. The ghost he talks to (Agatha, per the recaps) is not named in any source I can confirm, so the step leaves her out. Wikipedia places the closing dinner at his home in Eastview; he is not confirmed on screen there. Episode 8 has no transcript: its steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and the Wikipedia summary.

vq_steps: On a transfer bus to Saint Mabyn's, Lisa steals a guard's keys and escapes with Thomas, and the two become partners.
Lisa works London crowds with Thomas until Paladin makes her face a wall and takes him.
Lisa nicks suits and invitations to sneak Vision and Thomas into Katerina Wells's gala, then spots the killer arriving.
Lisa trails Ultron in Vision's body onto a cargo plane, then teams up with the real Vision to save Thomas.
In Madripoor, Lisa steals Paladin's van with Thomas and kisses him, before Jocasta takes her mind with a nanobot.
The nanobot wakes and turns Lisa on Thomas and Paladin, until Vision rewrites it with the source code.
Able to talk to drones through her nanobot, Lisa helps free Vision, then goes to work beside Paladin and E.D.I.T.H.
existing.notes: Old step was two sentences, over length, and called him Tommy where the screen has Thomas; split into story order (the Christmas 2027 bus, ep 2, comes before ep 1). Not in ep 3. The guard whose keys she takes is Clancy (credited; name not said in the transcript). The ep 8 work with Paladin has no name on screen I can confirm, so Independent holds. Episode 8 has no transcript: its steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and the Wikipedia summary.

vq_steps: Fiona employs Vision at her Edinburgh pub and is killed when Paladin's mercenaries attack it.
existing.notes: Kept as is: right, and her whole part is ep 1 (only mentioned in ep 2). Wikipedia calls her the owner; the MCU wiki calls her an employee; on screen she closes up and hands Vision the keys, so 'employs' holds either way. The shot is Snipey's.

vq_steps: J.A.R.V.I.S. runs security in Vision's Mindspace, warns him of a data leak, and talks him through the attack on the pub.
J.A.R.V.I.S. lives in Vision's mind with Tony's other AIs, then deletes himself to save Vision from Paladin.
existing.notes: Old step kept as the ep 2 step. After ep 2 he is only a photo at his funeral (ep 3), archive footage (ep 7) and mentions. Proto-One, the first aware A.I. Jo Carrington's team wakes in ep 6, is folded into J.A.R.V.I.S. by the MCU wiki, but the screen only calls it 'the base code for us' (the label Proto One is a subtitle speaker tag), so no J.A.R.V.I.S. step claims it.

vq_steps: F.R.I.D.A.Y. coaches Vision on small talk in his Mindspace and tries to calm him after the attack on the pub.
F.R.I.D.A.Y. traces Paladin's line of bounty hunters and backs Vision as he walks into the trap at Saint Mabyn's.
Taking over J.A.R.V.I.S.'s repairs, F.R.I.D.A.Y. mourns failing to save Tony and reveals Stark's AIs are based on real people.
F.R.I.D.A.Y. chases the Butcherbird Killer's trail into Interpol, and learns she is modeled on Howard Stark's aide Allison Hogan.
Locked in the attic, F.R.I.D.A.Y. fights against dropping the firewall, then chases Ultron out of Vision's mind alone.
Disguised as a bot in Jocasta's Mindspace, F.R.I.D.A.Y. calls E.D.I.T.H. to warn her of the nanobot plan.
F.R.I.D.A.Y. shadows Jocasta and Ultron into Jo Carrington's memories, until Ultron casts her out.
Spared by Ultron, F.R.I.D.A.Y. knocks on the door of Vision's sitcom, then leaves his Mindspace with the other AIs.
existing.notes: Old step ('lives in Vision's mind ... helps Vision protect Tommy', tagged ep 3) was too general to stand as an ep 3 step next to the new ones, so it is replaced; no place is tied to it. Allison Hogan is named by E.D.I.T.H. in ep 4. Where the AIs go when they leave the Mindspace in ep 8 is not clear in the recaps. Episode 8 has no transcript: its steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and the Wikipedia summary.

vq_steps: E.D.I.T.H., the thrill seeker of Vision's Mindspace, crashes in from a skydive and calls his skylight exit from the pub.
E.D.I.T.H. spots the tactical boots and earpieces that give away Paladin's mercenaries at Saint Mabyn's.
E.D.I.T.H. learns Stark's AIs are modeled on real people and holds a funeral for J.A.R.V.I.S. in the Mindspace.
E.D.I.T.H. now lives in Vision's Mindspace, where she drives the Butcherbird Killer out of his mind.
In Stark's records, E.D.I.T.H. finds she is modeled on the widowed test pilot Edith Marks, and the killer on Jo Carrington.
E.D.I.T.H. helps rebuild Ultron's trail from Vision's memory and is left heartbroken when F.R.I.D.A.Y. chases after him.
E.D.I.T.H. urges Paladin's A.I. to break free, saves Vision and Paladin from his van, and turns his drones on the Ten Rings.
E.D.I.T.H. objects to the Client's map, but sees Vision off as he dives into his own code.
E.D.I.T.H. gets Paladin clear before his van is blown up, talks him into saving Vision, and joins Vision's sitcom.
E.D.I.T.H. leaves Vision's Mindspace to work with Paladin and Lisa as they start over.
existing.notes: This is the A.I. character entry (tm Stark Industries, statuses Active). Old step kept as step 3 (ep 4). Ep 8 role (saving Paladin, the sitcom, leaving with Paladin and Lisa) rests on the recaps and Wikipedia ('reform with E.D.I.T.H.'s guidance'); no group name is given for that work. Episode 8 has no transcript: its steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and the Wikipedia summary.

Collection object: Tony's E.D.I.T.H. glasses. Its old VisionQuest step (holder Vision) described the A.I. character, which has its own Compound file, and COLL_FORMAT leaves out AIs that are characters. Confirmed the glasses never appear new in VisionQuest: the MCU wiki lists Tony Stark's Glasses only as footage in ep 1 (reused footage), no transcript or recap mentions them, and the wiki's only glasses in eps 1, 3, 6, 7 and 8 are Paladin's Glasses; the pair Tommy wears to talk to Vision in ep 8 is never called Stark's. Step dropped.

vq_steps: Dum-E and U live in Vision's mind as handymen alongside Tony's other AIs.
Dum-E and U patch Vision up after Paladin's rounds, and at J.A.R.V.I.S.'s funeral Dum-E reads a poem and U sings.
Seized for a moment by the Butcherbird Killer, Dum-E and U then help trace her victims to Markridge Biotech.
Dum-E and U help rebuild Ultron's trail from Vision's memory, then write the Client's contract into Vision's core.
Flying a drone, Dum-E and U find Tommy and Lisa, are pulled into Ultron's sitcom, and leave Vision's Mindspace.
existing.notes: Old step kept as step 0 (ep 1). Credited in all eight; eps 2 and 6 give them little of their own, so no separate step. Step 3 spans eps 5 to 7 (tagged 7). Episode 8 has no transcript: its steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and the Wikipedia summary.

vq_steps: The bounty hunter Paladin shoots Vision with adamantium rounds, mortally wounding him.
Virgil Horton shoots Jocasta with adamantium bullets, fatally wounding her.
existing.notes: One step per holder change, per the Collection rule. Paladin also wears adamantium chest armor from the Ten Rings (ep 3) and still carries adamantium slugs in Madripoor (ep 6), same holder and status, so no extra step. The ep 8 bullets rest on the Laughing Place and GamesRadar recaps; the wiki lists Adamantium Bullet and Paladin Suit under ep 8 items.

vq_steps: Beneath the fallen Mount Wundagore, a hooded figure orders the Scarlet Witch to awaken, and Wanda opens her eyes.
existing.notes: No VisionQuest steps before. New footage, so kept: the second scene after the ep 8 credits replays her end in Multiverse of Madness (archive), then a hooded figure says 'Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine' and she opens her eyes and jolts awake (Laughing Place; Wikipedia cast and MCU wiki both list her as an uncredited cameo, not archive). Eps 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 are WandaVision archive footage only. The figure is Doctor Doom only off screen (Wikipedia note), so the step does not name him. Status Active: her Raft file ends Deceased in Agatha All Along (her crushed body), which stays as the viewer knew it then (retcon rule); this step shows her alive and awake. Not At large (the scene shows her only waking under the rubble, not loose) and not Captive (nothing shows her held). The app also has a Compound wanda-maximoff (last step Missing, Multiverse of Madness); if both files stay, it needs the same step. Rests on the Laughing Place recap and Wikipedia.

add.k: Jo Carrington's vault of billions of nanobots
st: Jo Carrington's healing nanobots lie locked by her grave, and Jocasta opens five of the vault's six bio locks.
Virgil Horton reveals he holds the nanobots and plans to use them to make humanity calm and obedient.
Jocasta frees Ultron into the nanobots, and he builds a body and sends a swarm at London, then destroys all but a few.

new.notes: Kept: a central object on screen. Ep 7 shows the vault by Jo Carrington's grave ('Final resting place for Dr. Josephine Carrington and her children'), bio keys one to five accepted and a sixth lock left; ep 8 has the nanobots in Virgil's room, Ultron's new body, the swarm on London and 'the now empty nest' (recaps). Named as the screen names it: 'in a nest' (ep 6, ep 7) and 'not the NEST' (ep 7, Jo's memory), so n is The NEST from its first step, with no invented earlier stage. Holder Jo Carrington in ep 7 is the screen's own framing (her grave, her 'children'). Step 1 is Secured (he keeps them, not yet deployed). The lone nanobot Jocasta puts in Lisa (eps 6, 7) is left to the people files. Ep 8 steps rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps and Wikipedia; the MCU wiki lists NEST and Nanites as ep 8 items.

dropped.name: Clancy
dropped.why: Re-tested, stays out. On screen only in ep 2, in two scenes: the guard who tasers inmates on the Saint Mabyn's bus, then at Saint Mabyn's he recognizes Thomas ('Jingle bells, I knew I'd see you again') and Paladin shoots him dead; ep 1 is only a photo. His name is never said (every 'Clancy' in the transcript is a subtitle label; Wikipedia's 'the guard Clancy' is from the credits) and no source says it is shown. Even named, his whole presence is one episode that turns on Thomas and Lisa's escape and Vision's rescue, and he is no one's family, spouse or boss. The bus escape and the guard's keys are in Tommy's and Lisa's files.

dropped.name: Horton's source code (Collection: horton-source-code)
dropped.why: Cut. Central to the plot but not an object on screen: it is code inside every synthetic's mind ('Within your very own source code'), and its steps are memories and Vision's subconscious (COLL_FORMAT: visions and dreams are not steps). J.I.M. says 'I don't have it', so the hand-over step was wrong, and Vision and Jocasta both carry it at once, so no chain of custody holds. Its story is told in the people files (Vision's ep 7 step here).
